name: Battle of Verdun

sides.name: French Second Army and Fortified Region of Verdun

units.name: German corps on the east bank
French guns on the west bank

phases.title: The German guns open on the east bank
phases.text: After delays from fog, rain and wind, a ten-hour bombardment began on the right bank, and the German corps attacked at 4:00 p.m. French XXX Corps held the north and north-east of the salient.

phases.title: The Germans take Bois des Caures
phases.text: German troops advanced about 5 km and took the wood after two French battalions had held it for two days. The French XXX Corps was forced out of its second line of defence.

phases.title: A German party enters Fort Douaumont
phases.text: Infantry reached their objectives in under twenty minutes, and two parties made for the fort. One of about 100 men found the ditch bunkers unmanned and took prisoner the small maintenance crew inside.

phases.title: The attack widens to the west bank
phases.text: Falkenhayn lent two divisions from the reserve, and the German VI and X Reserve Corps attacked towards Mort-Homme and Côte 304 to silence the French guns across the river. Those guns went on firing into the Germans on the east bank.

phases.title: The French attack Fort Douaumont
phases.text: After a bombardment begun on 17 May, the French attacked the fort. The 129th Infantry Regiment reached it in a few minutes and got in through the west and south sides, and by nightfall about half of the fort was recaptured.

phases.title: The French in the fort are cut off
phases.text: The 34th Division was sent to reinforce the French in the fort, but the attempt failed. German reserves cut off the French troops inside and forced them to surrender, and 1,000 French prisoners were taken.

phases.title: The top of Fort Vaux is occupied
phases.text: The German attack shifted back to the right bank, south of Fort Douaumont. After a final assault by about 10,000 men on 1 June, the top of Fort Vaux was occupied on 2 June.

phases.title: The garrison of Fort Vaux surrenders
phases.text: Fighting went on underground until the garrison ran out of water. The 574 survivors surrendered on 7 June, and when news reached Verdun the Line of Panic was occupied.

phases.title: Gas shells fall on the French guns
phases.text: German artillery fired over 116,000 Diphosgene gas shells at French artillery positions. They caused over 1,600 casualties and silenced many of the French guns.

phases.title: The German salient towards Fort Souville
phases.text: At 5:00 a.m. the Germans attacked on a front of 5 km and drove a salient of 3 by 2 km into the French defences. They came within 5 km of the Verdun citadel before the French recaptured Chapelle Sainte-Fine and the advance stopped.

phases.title: The attack on Fort Souville
phases.text: Three German divisions attacked, but the infantry bunched on the path to the fort and came under French artillery fire and under sixty machine-gunners who had come out of the fort. Thirty men reached the top on 12 July.

phases.title: The French retake Fort Douaumont
phases.text: After a six-day bombardment French divisions attacked on 20 October behind a creeping barrage. The Germans had partly evacuated Fort Douaumont, and French marines and colonial infantry recaptured it on 24 October.

phases.title: The Germans evacuate Fort Vaux
phases.text: An attempt on Fort Vaux failed, but the heaviest French artillery bombarded it for a week. On 2 November the Germans evacuated the fort, and by 5 November the French were back at the front line of 24 February.

note: This plan shows the whole operation from 21 February to 5 November 1916, not a single field: each block is an army, a corps or a group of divisions, and the forts, wood and hill are the places the accounts name. The positions of the blocks on the plan are approximate, and north is taken to be up because the accounts place the Germans north of Verdun and the right (east) bank of the Meuse on the right. The Meuse and the town are placed by judgement. The French counter-offensive of 15 to 17 December is not drawn, and neither is the fighting on the west bank after March.
